name: Red Pen — "check this" for anything anyone tells you
one_liner: Paste any figure-laden claim (a rival's answer, a Telegram tip) and get it marked up line by line — OK, wrong (with both sources named), different-basis, or honestly unverified — by running the app's own hostile-battery witnesses outward instead of only on itself.

sidecar/services/company_narrative.py:97 (_source_values — bare list[float], can only redact to [unverified])

sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:1469-1474 (catalog's one rule — a read_handler capability auto-projects to the external MCP surface)
new_parts: labelled source map (value -> {field, provider, as_of, url}) so every tick carries its receipt
rupee literacy in the token grammar: ₹, Rs, crore/lakh/lakh-crore scale words, Indian comma grouping (1,05,130)
four-state verdict (OK / X / BASIS / ?), with BASIS fed directly by existing witness conflicts
new check_claims capability, kind="read_handler", in catalog.py (auto-projects to MCP surface)
marked-up-text block in src/modules/research/brief-blocks.tsx
risk: A red pen that is wrong is worse than no red pen. Consolidated vs standalone, TTM vs FY, reported vs adjusted are all "different basis", not "wrong"; an [X] may only fire when the witness is the same basis and period and names its source and as-of date, otherwise the mark degrades to BASIS or ?. The default must be humility.

name: The Blind-Spot Ledger — the app writes its own limitation paragraph
one_liner: End every brief with a specific, numbered confession of what was not read or checked (pages skipped, lanes that failed, citations dropped, depth downgraded) instead of a generic disclaimer, assembled deterministically from signals the pipeline already computes and drops.

deterministic, zero LLM tokens, works on the keyless lane
risk: Boilerplate: if it prints on every brief it becomes a disclaimer nobody reads; it must print only non-trivial gaps, in one to four lines, with numbers.

name: The Scorecard — the first finance AI that keeps score on itself
one_liner: Persist every figure the agent states, with period/as-of/provider, and re-check it deterministically against later primary filings, so reopening a name later surfaces "my record on this name: 8 of 9 figures held" instead of a fresh, memory-less answer.

sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:344-353,402 (surfaced as PRIOR STATED VALUES in the preamble)
new_parts: sidecar claims.db (SQLite) keyed by symbol, each claim carrying period, as_of, provider, source_url
deterministic re-check on a new brief publish for the same symbol (same metric+period+different value = graded miss; different period = a change, not a miss)
read-only track_record capability
small Settings "Track record" page
risk: Grading unfairly in either direction. A price that moved is not an error; a restated prior-period figure is ambiguous. Only same-period, same-basis contradictions from a primary filing may count as a miss, and the page must show the denominator.

name: Page-anchored receipts and the Receipt Bundle
one_liner: Every figure in a brief hovers to its exact source page and quoted line and opens the PDF there; exporting a brief carries a manifest with URL, page, quote, fetch time and SHA-256 per figure, so a sceptical reader who does not own Vysted can verify it and a journalist can print it.

name: Audit Me — the shipped lie-detector test
one_liner: A command-palette "Trust audit", runnable with no API key at all, runs the app's own resolver, fundamentals and witnesses across a bundled set of names chosen to break it and publishes a report card of resolved-correctly / conflicts-disclosed / wrong-and-silent, with the failures printed in full.

new_parts: bundled fixture: a structural subset of the battery (identity, exchange, board, face value, scale, "has no NSE line"), fields that do not move daily, each with as_of

a report-card block, no LLM
doubles as the regression suite for idea 1 (Red Pen) and idea 7 (Receipt Bundle)
